author: san diego city wire
title: San Diego County issues second warning about recalled infant formula linked to botulism - San Diego City Wire
text:
County health officials in San Diego have issued a second reminder regarding the national recall of ByHeart Whole Nutrition Infant Formula, which has been linked to an outbreak of infant botulism. The outbreak has resulted in 37 cases across 17 states, including California, but no cases have been reported in San Diego County.
“It is really important that parents and caregivers check their baby’s formula and stop using any ByHeart formula products immediately,” said Dr. Sayone Thihalolipavan, M.D., M.P.H., County public health officer. “The FDA has received reports that some products could have remained on the shelves in multiple states so now is the time to double-check and discard any formula from this brand.”
County officials emphasized that there have been no reports of ByHeart formula still being sold locally. The Department of Environmental Health and Quality has worked with retailers since the initial recall announcement in mid-November to ensure removal of the product from store shelves and continued outreach to local businesses this week.
ByHeart initiated a voluntary recall on November 8 for certain lots of its infant formula, expanding it on November 11 to include all ByHeart formula products.
Health authorities advise anyone with unopened ByHeart formula at home to discard it and not use it. If an infant has consumed some of the recalled formula and there is still an open container at home, the FDA recommends photographing or recording package information (including brand and lot number), sealing it, labeling it “do not use,” and storing it for 30 days in case testing by health officials becomes necessary.
Parents or caregivers whose infants show symptoms after consuming ByHeart formula are urged to seek medical attention right away. Infant botulism is rare but serious, primarily affecting babies under six months old. It can cause difficulty breathing, muscle paralysis, and even death. Symptoms may appear as early as three days after exposure but typically develop within 10 to 30 days; they include constipation, poor feeding, weak crying, loss of head control, and trouble swallowing.
To further alert healthcare providers locally, County Public Health officials issued a California Health Alert Network notification for San Diego County on November 12. Officials continue working with regional healthcare providers to watch for clinical signs of infant botulism and report suspected cases to state health authorities.
Anyone with concerns related to this health alert should contact their healthcare provider immediately.
